subject: RFP: Commercial breakdown request — token bands, true-up cadence, and crediting

Subject: RFP commercial appendix — ask on token banding and true-up cadence

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for agreeing to respond to the commercial appendix of our RFP. Procurement has a few follow-ups so we can evaluate total cost of ownership across three deployment scenarios: hosted (API), dedicated reserve, and private (VPC). Specifically we need:

- A clear token unit price table by monthly committed tier (bands) for 6 commit levels.
- Treatment of unused committed tokens (carry-forward, credits, or forfeiture).
- True-up cadence: monthly vs quarterly vs annual reconciliation and any associated billing lag.
- Overage calculation(s) and incremental price per token above the band.
- Any volume-based credits or smoothing protections (e.g., grace bands, burst cushions).

Can you provide a short playbook and attach a sample pricing schedule we can use in our cost model? We have a deadline of 2026-03-12 for the commercial scoring team.

Appreciate it — if it's easier, a quick call early next week would work.

Best,
Sara Nguyen
Head of Procurement, GlobeChem

Sara —

Thanks for the clear list. Attaching a concise playbook and an initial pricing schedule for your modelers. High level summary below; full detail in the XLSX.

Summary (high level):
- Commit bands: 6 monthly tiers (10M, 25M, 50M, 100M, 250M, 500M tokens). Per-token price decreases stepwise by band.
- Unused commit treatment: 3-month carry-forward for hosted API and Dedicated; Private option is handled via billing credit applied at true-up (no cash-back).
- True-up cadence options: monthly (default for hosted), quarterly (common for Dedicated), annual true-up available for enterprise contracts with forecast-based smoothing.
- Overage: billed at an incremental rate tied to committed band (e.g., +12% over band unit price for first 10% overage, then flat incremental thereafter).
- Grace bands: optional 5% operational cushion for launches (one-time, front-loaded) or rolling 3-month smoothing for seasonal patterns.

I'm looping in Marissa for pricing rationale and Karthik for the overage math. If you can confirm which deployment(s) GlobeChem cares about most, we'll prioritize the tabs in the spreadsheet.

Attachments: [Attachment: Redwood_Pricing_Schedule_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

Quick clarifying note for GlobeChem and procurement:

- The carry-forward window we propose is intended to be protective but predictable: unused monthly commit can roll forward up to 3 months and then expires. That balances flexibility and forecast discipline.
- For Dedicated contracts with annual commitments we can offer a true-up that reconciles actuals vs committed at the end of each quarter with a nettable credit applied against the next invoice.
- Private (on-prem / VPC) customers commonly prefer invoice-level credits rather than token refunds; legal prefers credits to reduce cash movement.

Karthik — can you confirm an example overage math for the 50M band (illustrative) so GlobeChem can plug into their model?

Sara — feel free to ping if you want two scenarios: (A) aggressive smoothing (quarterly true-up + 10% grace band) and (B) conservative (monthly true-up + 5% one-time launch cushion). We'll include both in the attached workbook.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Sr. Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Sara / team —

Attaching the illustrative calculations referenced during the thread and a short notes tab in the spreadsheet. Key example (50M monthly band):

- Committed unit price (50M band): $0.0018 per token.
- Overage tiers: first 10% over band billed at $0.00202 per token (+12%); remaining overage billed at $0.00232 (+29%).
- Example reconciliation (monthly true-up): if actual = 60M tokens, charge = (50M * $0.0018) + (5M * $0.00202) + (5M * $0.00232) subject to minimum billing protections.
- Carry-forward: up to 15M tokens may be applied from previous three months; any residual overage billed per above.
- Credits: for annual enterprise commitments we apply a volume discount schedule that yields effective blended prices 6–14% lower relative to monthly list depending on committed term. Details in the XLSX.

Attachments: [Attachment: Redwood_Pricing_Schedule_v2.xlsx (spreadsheet)]

Let us know if GlobeChem prefers quarterly true-ups for modeling — we can produce a pro forma with sample cash flows and invoice timing (important for procurement scorecard).

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Commercial Finance, Redwood Inference
